🔊 Shia Jurist Grand Ayatollah Vahid Khorasani passes away

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Grand Ayatollah Hossein Vahid Khorasani, a leading Shia source of emulation and prominent Islamic jurist, has passed away, his office announced on Tuesday.

A statement released by his office expressed deep sorrow over the death of the senior cleric, describing him as a distinguished scholar and a leading teacher at Islamic seminaries.
​
It said Vahid Khorasani had devoted decades to studying, researching, and teaching Islamic sciences, defending the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad’s infallible households, supporting orphans, training numerous scholars, and promoting religious traditions, particularly mourning ceremonies.
​
The statement offered condolences to Imam Mahdi (12th Shia Imam), Islamic seminaries, followers of religious scholarship and authority, and Shias worldwide. Details of his funeral, burial, and memorial ceremonies will be announced later.
​
Born on March 21, 1921, in Neyshabur, northeastern Iran, Vahid Khorasani began his religious education in Mashhad, where he studied under prominent scholars before advancing to higher studies in jurisprudence and Islamic principles.
​
After receiving authorization for independent jurisprudential judgment, he moved to Najaf, Iraq, at the age of 27 to further his studies. He attended the classes of leading scholars, including Grand Ayatollah Abolqasem Khoei, whose jurisprudential school significantly influenced his approach. He also attended Imam Khomeini’s lectures during his stay in Najaf.
​
In 1958, he began teaching jurisprudence and Islamic principles in Najaf, continuing for nearly 12 years. He returned to Iran in 1970, initially teaching in Mashhad before moving to Qom later that year.
